s1.syndrome_frame: Severe lower limb deformity and pain with abnormal bone density and laboratory findings
salient_findings: Osteopenia of the left femoral head
key_facts: Patient is a 32-year-old woman
Patient has severe left knee pain
Patient has bilateral genu valgum deformity
Patient had trochanteric bursitis at age 22
Patient takes OTC vitamin D3 without calcium
Patient's Q-angle was 17° at age 22 and 23° currently
Patient has osteopenia of the left femoral head
Patient has normal lumbar spine density
Patient has low serum phosphate
Patient has elevated total 25-hydroxyvitamin D and 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D
Patient has low parathyroid hormone
Patient has undetectable FGF23
Patient has inappropriately normal phosphate excretion
Patient has bilateral medullary nephrocalcinosis without stones

shortlist.label: X-linked hypophosphatemia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has severe lower limb deformity, low serum phosphate, and inappropriately normal phosphate excretion, consistent with X-linked hypophosphatemia

shortlist.label: Hereditary hypophosphatemic rickets with hypercalciuria
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has hypophosphatemia, elevated vitamin D levels, and bilateral medullary nephrocalcinosis, which are features of hereditary hypophosphatemic rickets with hypercalciuria

shortlist.label: Autosomal dominant hypophosphatemic rickets
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has hypophosphatemia, osteopenia, and abnormal bone density, which are consistent with autosomal dominant hypophosphatemic rickets

shortlist.label: Dent disease
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has hypophosphatemia, low parathyroid hormone, and bilateral medullary nephrocalcinosis, which are features of Dent disease

shortlist.label: Vitamin D-dependent rickets type 1
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has hypophosphatemia, elevated vitamin D levels, and osteopenia, which are consistent with vitamin D-dependent rickets type 1

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of bilateral genu valgum deformity, low serum phosphate, and history suggestive of rickets, along with the laboratory findings of low serum phosphate, elevated vitamin D levels, and low parathyroid hormone, are consistent with X-linked hypophosphatemia. The presence of osteopenia and the patient's response to vitamin D3 supplementation without calcium also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Hereditary hypophosphatemic rickets with hypercalciuria
rejected.why: The patient's normal urine calcium excretion does not support this diagnosis, which typically presents with hypercalciuria.

rejected.label: Autosomal dominant hypophosphatemic rickets
rejected.why: The patient's undetectable FGF23 levels are not typical for this condition, which often presents with elevated FGF23.

rejected.label: Dent disease
rejected.why: The patient's lack of significant proteinuria and the presence of bilateral medullary nephrocalcinosis without stones do not strongly support this diagnosis, which typically includes significant proteinuria and other renal manifestations.

rejected.label: Vitamin D-dependent rickets type 1
rejected.why: The patient's elevated 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D levels do not support this diagnosis, which typically results from a deficiency in the enzyme responsible for converting 25-hydroxyvitamin D to 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D, leading to low levels of 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D.
